text:
alice: Quick sync — we need a short spec for the continuous batching signals we want the runtime to emit for the console/telemetry team. I sketched a few ideas but want alignment before we start instrumenting and exploding our ingest costs.

jason: +1. Can you list the minimal set to unblock dashboards? we should avoid high-cardinality fields at first.

alice: Minimal (proposal):
- `redwood.batch.size` histogram (per-request batch size)
- `redwood.batch.wait_ms` histogram (time a request waited for batch)
- `redwood.queue.saturation` gauge (0..1, per-worker-group)
- `redwood.backpressure.events` counter (increment on backpressure/fallback)
Also tag by `model`, `route`, `region`, and `priority` (low/normal/high). Keep `customer_id` out for now.

maya: Runtime can emit histograms w/ predefined buckets. Prefer histogram over quantile metrics so infra can calculate stable p50/p95 without extra runtime work.
Example buckets for wait_ms: [0,1,2,5,10,25,50,100,250,500,1000,5000]
For batch.size: [1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128]

rajan: FYI ingest cost will spike if we include `route`+`model`+`region`+`priority` for every metric. Suggest we start with `model`+`route` and shard sampling: 10% global sampling for histograms and 100% for saturation gauges/backpressure counters.

lee: From console UX POV we want:
- heatmap: batch size distribution across routes (time bucketed)
- latency waterfall: wait_ms p50/p95/p99 per model
- saturation dial: per-worker-group colored by threshold (green/yellow/red)
- alerting: when p95(wait_ms) > 200ms for 5m or queue_saturation > 0.8
So we really need consistent tag names and stable bucketization.

sara: Also need rollouts-friendly views: when we flip routing policy (latency-first -> cost-first), we want to compare pre/post distributions for the targeted routes. Would be ideal to have `rollout_id` tag passed through in canary windows.

jason: Hmm `rollout_id` adds cardinality, but useful for short windows. Maybe only emit `rollout_id` when ENV var `REDWOOD_EMIT_ROLLOUT_TAG` is set (enabled for canary hosts) and default off.

maya: Implementable. Two implementation notes:
1) histograms emitted with default sampling=1.0, but telemetry pipeline will drop to 0.1 sampling unless `REDWOOD_FULL_TELEMETRY` is set for canaries.
2) we will emit an aggregated `redwood.batch.size_sum` and `_count` for quick dashboarding (prom-style) so we don't always need histogram decoding.

rajan: Make sure we have a cardinality cap check in the emit path. If unique tag combinations in 1m > 1000 for a given worker-group, throttle `rollout_id` and `route` tags and emit a `redwood.cardinality.throttle` counter.

lee: UX wants the raw histogram buckets in metrics store so frontend can compute percentiles client-side for interactive charts. Can infra guarantee buckets are preserved after downsampling?

rajan: We'll preserve buckets for sampled docs only. For downsampled docs we keep `_sum`/`_count` and a small 8-bucket sketch. We'll document behavior in the telemetry contract.

alice: Sounds like consensus: histograms + sum/count + saturation gauge + backpressure counter. Tags: model, route, region, priority. Optional rollout_id gated by env + sampling. Action items:
- rajan: add cardinality throttle + sampling knobs in telemetry agent (PR)
- maya: runtime emits histograms + sum/count + gauges (impl PR)
- jason: dashboard panels + alert rules (draft PR)
- lee: console UX mockups (small heatmap + saturation dial)

tora-bot: PRs linked: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/1789 (telemetry-agent), https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/1792 (runtime-histograms)

sara: timeline? product wants visible dashboards for the canary next week (Wed). Is that realistic?

maya: Maybe if we scope canary to 1 model + 2 routes and enable `REDWOOD_EMIT_ROLLOUT_TAG` there — should be doable by Tue night.

jason: I'll mock the dashboard with synthetic data and push a dashboard PR today. If runtime PR lands by EOD Mon we can wire real metrics.

rajan: I'll start the telemetry-agent PR today and add the sampling knob + cardinality throttle. ETA EOD Mon.

lee: I'll share quick Figma by tomorrow morning with the heatmap + dial. Keeping interactions minimal so we can ship.

alice: Great. Follow-ups: confirm final bucket lists in the runtime PR and add a short section in docs/telemetry.md describing sampling, rollout tag gating, and cardinality throttle behavior.

maya: will add buckets to PR and a short doc snippet.

jason: tagging @sara for product visibility. Anything else?

sara: please add an alerting playbook blurb for ops: who to page when saturation triggers and recommended rollback steps.

alice: noted. Thanks everyone. We'll reconvene if any blocker appears. :thumbsup:
